previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and PEG dependence was admitted from a skilled nursing facility for fever and vomiting. Workup revealed a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus urinary tract infection and possible aspiration-related pneumonia. He was treated with linezolid for the VRE UTI and cefepime for the lung infection, with clinical improvement. A CT scan showed bladder wall thickening and diverticula, raising concern for chronic urinary retention; a Foley catheter was placed as he did not tolerate intermittent catheterization, and outpatient urodynamic testing was scheduled. A pressure- and moisture-related rash on the back was treated with topical steroids and antifungal powder. He completed a 7-day antibiotic course, remained stable, and was discharged to extended care with instructions to continue oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis, maintain the Foley catheter until urology follow-up, and resume all chronic medications including antiretrovirals and seizure prophylaxis.

# ___ malfunction
Patient with chronic GJ tube, who initially presented with GJ 
tube malfunction.  Initially it was addressed at the bedside in 
the ED by ___, who changed external tubing and was able to flush 
the tube without issue.  The Jtube portion then clogged again 
following admission (see below re: why patient was admitted), 
but then was addressed by nursing with bedside maneuvers. 
Patient was subsequently monitored x 24 hours to make sure that 
tube functioned without issue.  In the future, would administer 
medications via Gtube, tube feeds via Jtube, and flush as 
ordered, to reduce risk of future clogging. 

# Fever
Patient was admitted after developing isolated fever in the ED.  
In the ED patient was started on empiric antibiotics for 
presumed UTI.  On admission, given UA only had few bacteria, and 
the patient had absence of leukocytosis (as had been seen with 
prior infections) or other systemic signs of infection, this was 
felt to be bacterial colonization in setting of indwelling 
catheter.  Additionally, per patient's sister, initial sign of 
infection for patient is encephalopathy--patient was not 
encephalopathic.  Remainder of workup for infection was 
negative.  All antibiotics were held after admission and patient 
was monitored x 48 hours without signs of evolving infection. 

# History of Cdiff
Given his history of cdiff, and that he received antibiotics in 
the ED, he was restarted on PO vancomycin prophylaxis to prevent 
Cdiff recurrence, with plan for 1 week of therapy (last day = 
___.

patient developed hypoglycemia.  Patient responded to 
hypoglycemia protocol.  When tube feeds were restarted
